title: Kernel cohorting and lightweight prefill/decode sample collector
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Implement a low-overhead in-process sampler that cohorts requests by kernel version / kernel implementation and emits compact per-kernel telemetry for prefill and decode flows. Goal: enable principled kernel-selection heuristics and attention-pathway analysis without adding measurable latency to production requests.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler injects NVTX ranges and canonical span tags for sampled requests with <1% p95 latency overhead in synthetic bench
Collected events include kernel_id, kernel_variant, seq_len, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, exec_us, cuda_stream_id, and lightweight attention_hint metadata
Daily aggregated cohort-level reports render in Console and match local offline reconstructions for >=99% of sampled traces
Sampling configuration is adjustable via runtime flags (rate, cohort-keys, burn-in window) and can be toggled per-tenant
implementation_notes: Run a tiny per-worker ring buffer of sampled trace envelopes; flush async to telemetry worker to avoid blocking hot path
Use stable kernel identifier composed of (model_family, kernel_impl_hash, cuda_arch, quant_mode) to form cohorts
Annotate NVTX ranges with short integer keys for span alignment in the trace store (nvtx_key -> span_id) instead of long strings
Add prefill/decode lightweight counters in the runtime so we can correlate token-level peaks with kernel switches
Fallback to a minimal metric emission (prometheus counter + histogram) when trace backend unavailable
sampling_strategy: Adaptive reservoir sampling: maintain per-cohort reservoir with target samples/day proportional to cohort traffic
Initial burn-in: sample 5% of requests for new kernel variants for 24h to collect baseline metrics
Mutation detector: on sudden exec_time regression >20% for a cohort, escalate sampling rate for that cohort for 1 hour
Max global sampling cap to bound telemetry cost (configurable per environment)
decisions: Prefer in-process lightweight envelopes + async uploader vs synchronous trace writes to minimize tail latency impact
Canonicalize NVTX naming to short integer tags to reduce metadata size and speed span stitching in trace queries
Store full verbose per-kernel stack only for sampled traces; emit compact aggregate histograms for all cohorts
Expose cohort definitions and sampling knobs through Console for SRE/Platform teams
tradeoffs: Higher sampling for anomaly cohorts increases telemetry cost but accelerates root-cause; chosen mutation detector is tuned conservative
In-process buffering reduces blocking risk but shifts memory pressure to worker; ring buffer size tuned experimentally
Canonical NVTX keys improve performance of trace joins but make raw trace logs less human-readable without a decoder
prototype_results: Canary bench (gpt-2-like model): reservoir sampler overhead measured at +0.4% p95 latency; avg exec_time_us variance correctly captured
Detected a kernel fallback path in variant 'matmul_v3q' that increased avg exec_time_us by 28% for seq_len>2048 in canary traffic
Baseline cohort histograms matched offline profiler within 2% for mean exec_time and within 5% for 95th percentile
retention_and_export: Sample envelopes retained in-process up to 60s and forwarded to trace/metric pipeline asynchronously
Export compact metrics to metrics backend (histograms/counters) and sampled spans to trace backend; full traces gated by sampling decision
Retention of sampled traces set to 30d by default; cohort aggregates retained 90d
Option to route PII-free envelopes to external observability providers via customer-configured endpoints
blockers: Need final approval for NVTX key schema from tracing team
Temporary rate-limits in telemetry pipeline causing dropped envelopes in staging
Permissions for per-tenant sampling toggles in Console API not yet exposed
